title: a verdict re-runs a red alone and records a contention red beside it
intention: A verdict re-runs a red reading once, alone, after its pooled runs drain; both readings stand, and a red that turns green alone is a contention red that is recorded and does not refuse. A WATCHME brings cc_0 every re-run's pair of readings to review the hypothesis.
why: Measured 2026-11-16 (Q#119): e56a68e651c2 runs a verdict's instruments three at a time; each sealed run gets its own ~/.cairn, but the repo, /tmp, the network and git are shared by all three, so a red can come from a neighbour rather than from the proof. Akien answered 2026-11-18 that CC's choice is a hypothesis with a WATCHME back to cc_0 (outline 0.6.1, 9.4.8.1.1). Split out of e56a68e651c2 when the cast door's shape check refused 11 outcomes on one plan.
traces_to: Law 3: nothing is known until measured; outline 0.6.1 and 9.4.8.1.1.
how: HYPOTHESIS (outline 9.4.8.1.1, 0.6.1): a red at width 3 may be a neighbour's. In observe_instruments, after e56a68e651c2's pool has drained, each reading whose run disagrees with its expect_exit is re-run once, alone, with nothing else in flight; the reading keeps run and gains run_alone, contention (true when the alone run agrees) and neighbours (the readings whose started/ended interval overlapped its first run). _observed_entries judges a contention reading by its alone run, so a contention red does not refuse and a red that disagrees alone too refuses as before. The WATCHME probe reads post-era verdict berths and returns the pairs and totals for cc_0. BUILDME waits on e56a68e651c2, whose pool and started/ended epochs this composes.

a red that agrees alone is marked contention true and the verdict does not refuse on it; a red that disagrees alone too is marked contention false and refuses as before
